text:
mike.j: Hey security — got a weird SMS earlier from +1 (555) 123-9999 saying "invoice attached" and the calendar auto-created an event called 'Payment Review'. I clicked the SMS link once (yep, I know...) around 09:12am and then removed the calendar invite. Link: https://payl0ad[.]cloud/rt/ab12
sara.sec: Thanks — can you drop screenshots of the SMS and the calendar invite? Did you enter creds or download anything?
mike.j: screenshot attached (see thread). didn't enter creds, no download. calendar had a zoom link that 404'd. I did paste the link into a private browser tab to see headers only.
threat-bot: Sandbox detonation complete for artifact https://payl0ad.cloud/rt/ab12
threat-bot: Verdict: MALICIOUS. Observed: obfuscated JS redirect -> staged payload -> exfil POST to s3-eu-west-1[.]upload-cdn[.]info (tcp 443). Dropped payload: invoice.pdf.dll (exe disguised)
raj-sre: Block domain at gateway and WAF: payl0ad.cloud and upload-cdn.info. Also add to network denylist and endpoint blocking rules. Can infra rotate sessions for any service accounts that might have been accessed?
elaine-hr: Noted — I'll email the users who got the calendar invite and ask them to report if they clicked. We'll push org-wide notice about the SMS. For the user who clicked (mike.j) recommend MFA re-issue and password reset. I'll coordinate with IT.
sara.sec: I ran hunter search across corp logs for outbound POST to upload-cdn.info between 08:00-12:00 UTC. Found 3 distinct client IPs: 18.205.32.11, 34.201.12.77, 100.64.23.10. Those last one internal NAT. Starting containment: 1) block domains 2) isolate affected endpoints 3) rotate any tokens seen in logs 4) open incident ticket.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2147. Pager duty on-call: raj-sre
raj-sre: Taking lead on containment. Taking the two endpoints offline now and pulling full disk images. Also pushing NAC block for the internal IP 100.64.23.10
mike.j: thx — my endpoint ping is down, let me know if you need it back for forensics.
sara.sec: Sandbox artifacts uploaded to the case: md5: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e, yara: matched 3 rules (obf-js, masquerade-exe, s3-exfil)
elaine-hr: Sent notification to affected users + reset instructions. Template used: https://docs.internal/incidents/sms-phish-template
sara.sec: Post-incident actions: 1) Request vendor to block sender numbers at SMS gateway. 2) Add calendar invite verification in sync rules to ignore auto-subscribed invites from unknown senders. 3) Run company-wide SMS phishing micro-training next week.
raj-sre: Also recommend we add an alert for calendar event creation that includes external domains and auto-accepted invites. I'll file a ticket with eng-platform.
mike.j: sorry everyone, lesson learned. Happy to join the training.
elaine-hr: We'll follow up with a short acknowledgement email and close after root cause + containment confirmed.
sara.sec: Closing notes: IOCs = payl0ad.cloud, upload-cdn.info, +15551239999, invoice.pdf.dll. Recommended severity: LOW-MED (no creds exfil observed but active payload). Assign postmortem owner: sara.sec
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-2147 status: CONTAINED -> follow-ups pending
sara.sec: I'll open the postmortem doc and add timeline. Link: https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-2147
elaine-hr: Added training enrollment for all staff for next Wed.
raj-sre: I'll follow up on domain block propagation in cloud provider and WAF tomorrow morning.
